Loss-of-function mutations in GRHL2 disrupt its role in epithelial development and differentiation, leading to a spectrum of phenotypes including hearing impairment (Disease A), and nail abnormalities, abnormal teeth morphology, palmoplantar keratoderma, and oral hyperpigmentation (Disease B).

**How to falsify it:** The presence of a pathogenic variant in GRHL2 with a demonstrable gain-of-function mechanism or a distinct causal gene for either disease would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs117640346)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of GRHL2 in these distinct disease phenotypes could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting epithelial development pathways for both hearing loss and ectodermal dysplasia syndromes.
